title: Seeds, Cuttings and Tissue Culture as Propagation Systems
summary: Seed propagation, vegetative cuttings and tissue culture preserve or generate genetic variation in different ways and therefore require different expectations for identity, sanitation and establishment.

sections.title: Seeds create genetically distinct offspring
sections.body: Sexual reproduction combines parental genetic material through segregation and recombination. Even siblings from the same cross can therefore differ substantially, especially when parents are heterozygous and target traits have complex genetic architecture.

sections.title: Cuttings preserve a donor genotype but not a sterile state
sections.body: Vegetative cuttings are clones of the donor genotype, yet propagation success still depends on donor condition, sanitation, rooting environment and acclimatization. Clonal identity does not by itself guarantee pathogen-free material or uniform performance across environments.

sections.title: Tissue culture expands control and complexity
sections.body: In-vitro micropropagation can support rapid multiplication and germplasm management, but genotype-by-medium effects, contamination, passage history and culture-associated genetic or epigenetic variation require stronger process control and fidelity monitoring.
